messages:
Maya: heads up — after the 10:15 canary rollout a subset of canary pods in eu-west started crashlooping. Not full prod, but ~20% error rate in inference path for a minority of hosts. logs show init container failing on a healthcheck change.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: Ben — high severity alert triggered for service=inference-canary eu-west (alert id: A-90821). Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/canary-failure

Ben: Ack — I'm on it. Maya, can you paste the failing init logs? Is this the new init config that touches mounts?

Maya: copying a snippet from one of the pods:
```
InitContainer error: exit status 1
2024-06-25T10:16:12Z ERROR: mount script failed: permission denied when creating /var/lib/model-cache
Stack: /bin/sh: line 42: cannot create /var/lib/model-cache: Permission denied
```
Looks like the init tries to create a cache dir with root-owned mount but the pod runs as non-root under the new securityContext change from the manifest. We added fsGroup recently.

Ben: hm. That would crash the init and trigger a restart loop — also HPA saw increased CPU while pods churned. Customer impact: some inference requests returned 503s (partial degraded routing to canary). I flagged support with a note.

Julia: I see customer reports from EU region in the dashboard — a handful of mid-tier customers affected (requests per minute down ~18% for eu-west). No billing impact yet. Recommend stop the rollout and either rollback or throttle traffic.

Ben: Agreed. Options: 1) Abort canary / scale canary ->0 to drain traffic, or 2) toggle feature flag kill-switch (we have per-customer routing) to bypass canary and route to stable model. Which is faster?

Maya: feature flag is fastest. I'll trigger it but need ops or SRE rights to flip global routing.

Ben: @Julia can you flip the flag? It's under Console -> Feature Flags -> rollout/eu-canary-weight. Set to 0.

Julia: flipping now.

incident-bot: FeatureFlag change recorded: rollout/eu-canary-weight set from 25 to 0 by Julia at 2024-06-25T10:18:45Z.

Julia: done. Observability shows traffic diverting to stable within ~30s. Error rate on the frontdoor for eu-west dropping. :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks. I'll prepare a quick rollback of the manifest to the previous commit where init didn't change. If we want to keep the new init we need to update securityContext and ensure directory exists with correct ownership.

Ben: go ahead with rollback as a safer immediate fix. Use the deploy CLI: `deploy-cli rollback inference-canary --to=20240624-rc3`

Maya: running rollback now. Logs from deployment:
```
deploy-cli: starting rollback to 20240624-rc3
k8s: scaling new-canary-deployment to 0 replicas
k8s: applying previous manifest 20240624-rc3
success: rollout complete for inference-canary (stable restored)
```

Maya: pods are stable and healthy. No more init errors on new pods.

Ben: Good. Julia — confirm customer-facing errors cleared?

Julia: dashboards show request success rate back to baseline in eu-west. Support updated customers to say we mitigated.

Sean: jumping in for post-mortem tracking. Maya, can you save the failing manifest and add a short blameless note for root cause? Looks like the manifest changed fsGroup and removed an explicit dir chown step in init script. We should catch with a pre-deploy smoke test.

Maya: will add an entry in the rollout PR and create a test that runs the init container as non-root in a dry-run cluster. Also will add a linter rule to flag fsGroup changes without dir ownership.

Ben: handoff: I'm going offline in ~15m — Sean will take ownership of monitoring for the next 4 hours. I'll leave runbook notes and the diffs in the incident thread.

Ben: notes: incident severity — S2 (partial customer impact, mitigated by feature flag + rollback). Time to detection ~2m (alerts), time to mitigation ~6m.

incident-bot: Incident A-90821 status: mitigated. Owner transferred to Sean. Next steps: postmortem required within 48h.

Sean: taking ownership. I'll open the postmortem doc and link the manifest and support thread. Thanks team. :pray:
